entries.notes: Reopened 2026-07-22 after the reporter reproduced the same loader crash on v0.6.2. Direct inspection of the published v0.6.4 arm64 APK proved libtine_lib.so still imported undefined renameat2: the first fix covered backup.rs but missed the Android-built model.rs trash path. entries.title: An advanced query is refused for a declared :result-transform only, and a BEGIN_QUERY payload's transform is no longer dropped
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B2 plus the synthesis false refusal (I-12, I-9). advanced_pred refused any query whose text contained the substring :result-transform, even in a title, string, comment or #_ discard; and inspect_begin_query dropped a real transform so the bare vector ran as a complete query. query_edn::declares_option now decides from the EDN reader, and the inspector carries the transform so the whole-query refusal names it. entries.title: A query row switched off with `-- ` never invalidates the active query
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B1. The stray-anchor and unquoted-relative-date reporters scanned the whole text and a refused-shape payload (@page placeholder) passed the per-row parse then failed the whole-query shape check, so a disabled row still produced an enabled diagnostic. Disabled lines are now masked (same byte length) before the reporters run and a forbidden-shape disabled payload is captured as a disabled raw capsule like any other malformed row.

entries.title: The query builder's date-bound preview resolves tokens exactly like the engine (-7D, 2026_01_05, the 10,000-year bound, year-0 month clamp)

coverage.scenario: resolveDateToken agrees with the native date-token golden; the_shared_date_token_golden_resolves_as_recorded

entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 mess finding / I-12 twin. dateExpr.ts re-implemented the Rust DateToken grammar: it accepted -7D and 7W, refused 2026_01_05 and 2026-1-5, accepted offsets past 10,000 years (NaN for huge ones), accepted Jan 1, 2022 / double spaces, and clamped 0000-01-31 +1m to Feb 28 (JS constructor remaps years 0-99). It now follows the engine grammar and both suites read tests/fixtures/i12-date-token-golden.json (Rust is authoritative). Not exposed through WASM: tine-core is not built for wasm32 and the preview must not wait on IPC.

entries.title: A TQL like ... escape 'c' clause is honoured (re-encoded to the one backslash convention) instead of silently ignored
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B7 (wrong results, no diagnostic). The lowering matched Expr::Like with escape_char ignored, so '100!%' escape '!' kept ! literal and % a wildcard. text::reencode_like_escape maps any single-character escape to the IR's backslash convention at parse time, so the printer needs no clause; a non-one-character escape is a Syntax diagnostic.

entries.title: A SCHEDULED:/DEADLINE: example inside a fenced block, or ending a longer word, does not schedule the block
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 / I-12 (eval.rs planning_text). The inline-planning fallback byte-scanned the raw block for the marker, so documentation in a fenced or #+BEGIN_ container and UNSCHEDULED: made a block a scheduled/deadline row. It now asks block_regions for the literal containers and requires a word boundary. Inline code stays eligible: the recorded og deviation (query_conformance) is unchanged.

entries.title: The 128-level outline admission uses lsdoc's fence-close rule, so an outline after an early-closed fence cannot bypass it
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L05 / I-12, I-22. parse_depth.rs treated a four-backtick opener as closed only by a same-character run of at least four, but lsdoc closes any fence at the NEXT marker line of either character (v2/source.rs is_fence_marker_line, find_matching_fence). A 129-deep outline between a shorter closer and a later stray opener was invisible to admission while the parser built the tree, and the recursive consumers (runtime ids, shrink) then walked it. The guard now transcribes lsdoc's rule; the test asks the parser for the real depth first. The remaining pre-parse guard is still a second grammar for fence ownership, now pinned by the parser-depth assertion.

entries.title: A legacy query table column and the render path normalise property keys exactly like the engine (space to hyphen, ASCII-only lowercase)

coverage.scenario: agrees with the engine's property key normaliser on the shared golden; the_shared_property_key_golden_normalises_as_recorded

entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 I-12 twin (legacyQueryTable.ts columnKey vs doc::property_key_norm). columnKey kept a space ('Owner Name' stayed 'owner name') and Unicode-lowercased, so a column named in query-properties:: missed the engine's key. One TS normaliser now lives in src/propertyKey.ts; render/block.ts re-exports it (a two-line edit outside the Q write set, recorded in the receipt); both suites read tests/fixtures/i12-property-key-norm-golden.json. Whether OG's Unicode lower-casing of non-ASCII keys should become the engine rule is a Rust-side product question left unchanged.

entries.title: The property-predicate reader no longer drops a second key or a nested atom test, and the builder's TS reader and LIKE helpers are pinned to the Rust ones by goldens

coverage.scenario: the_props_reader_answers_only_for_a_direct_key_shape; the_shared_props_reader_golden_reads_as_recorded; the_shared_like_escape_golden_encodes_and_decodes_as_recorded; twins agree with the native goldens

entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B5 plus the LIKE-escaping twin (I-12). Filter::props_key recursed into nested And and took the first of several keys, and props_atom_test then discarded the whole nested item, so any(props, key = 'a' and key = 'b') evaluated key a alone and And(And(key, x), y) lost x in every printer and in the evaluator. The reader now answers only for the direct section 3.3 shape (one direct key-equality item); anything else takes the general-predicate path the printers already have. queryBuilder.ts propsParts now mirrors the atom rule (several atoms form an and) and is exported; escapeLike/plainLikeSubstring are verified, not changed, against tests/fixtures/i12-like-escape-golden.json.

entries.title: Explaining an empty query result is linear in the conjunct count (one whole-filter probe past 64 conjuncts)
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3, I-22. explain_empty_plan built two probes per conjunct and the second cloned every OTHER conjunct plus the whole Query (source text included), so a 64 KB source of ~2,000 conjuncts made 4,000 probes of ~2,000 conjuncts each, which the evaluator then ran. EXPLAIN_MAX_CONJUNCTS = 64: beyond it the query is explained as one whole conjunct. Unit cost: plan size 2*N*(N-1) filter nodes before, N after, for N > 64; unchanged for N <= 64. Measured as the leaf count across probes in the test.

entries.title: The friendly page search keeps the best name matches when a content match competes for the last slot
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3 I-12 comparator twin. ScoredPage::is_better_than ranked a name match above a content match but Ord::cmp (the heap's eviction order) ranked the content match above it, so a full heap evicted the best name match. Now is_better_than and the result sort are derived from the one Ord. Unit cost: none (comparison only).

entries.title: The query memo charges the graph-wide tag-target set of a used_as_tag plan to its entry budget
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3 I-22. Plan::estimated_bytes omitted tag_targets, a per-plan graph-wide key set, so 64 retained used_as_tag entries could hold 64 copies outside the 64 MiB memo budget. Unit cost: one serialized-size pass over the set per retained entry, the same order as building it.

entries.title: Adding a page to a popular property key copies O(log holders) index nodes, not every holder's path
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3 I-25. Postings::applied cloned the whole BTreeSet<String> of a key's holders for every posting that moved, so an edit adding the first block property of a popular key to a page copied 10,000 paths on a 10k graph (facts_copies 10000, ceiling 256; measured with a temporary counter on the old code). Now a persistent PathSet: 1 copy, 80 shared-tree nodes on 10k vs 23 on 20 pages. Shape guard postings_are_persistent_sets_not_std_sets. Unit cost: bytes per edit unchanged for non-moving edits; a moving edit O(log holders). The lazy per-key registry re-derive that follows first registry use stays O(holders), inherent to rebuilding that key's rows.

entries.title: Copy / Export of a block query includes the page header property row the query view shows
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3 I-12. export_query_subtrees hydrated roots by walking Document::roots only, so the header property block (Hit::PageProperty, id page-property:...) that the query returned was counted as a vanished block and omitted. It is now rebuilt with page_property_block like the query does and flagged page_property. Unit cost: one header projection per page that has a wanted root.

entries.title: A query bounded by now is never served from the per-day answer memo
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3. The query memo files answers per day, but a created_at / last_modified_at bound spelled now resolves to the evaluation's milliseconds (OG time-ms), so a retained answer went stale within minutes and stayed stale until midnight. Plans that read the clock are returned but not retained; midnight-anchored tokens (today, -7d, -2h which OG anchors at UTC midnight) stay memoized. Unit cost: none.

entries.title: A save that moves no alias neither rebuilds nor re-walks the whole alias relation for each remembered backlinks answer
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 L02 B3 I-25. Each save re-judged every remembered backlinks / unlinked answer with equivalent_page_names, which rebuilt the neighbour map of ALL aliases per answer per document (10k aliases: 16.8 MB allocated by one text save; 177 KB now vs 355 KB for the no-alias control). AliasEdges indexes the alias relation once per generation and is carried by Arc across saves that moved no alias; the component walk is O(component). The alias list itself is carried by Arc too. Also ports master's page_hits_to_entries (an authored alias is offered under its own spelling on its owner's path, GH #482) which the phantom removal (REG-OG-GH623-ALIAS-353) needs; the existing quick_switch test now asserts master's owner-identity form. Checkpoint FORMAT 7 to 8 (memo entry bytes now charge the tag-target set; GOLDEN re-pinned from the measured digest). Unit cost: per save O(component) instead of O(aliases x answers); one O(aliases) index per generation lineage.

entries.title: The Display editor reads a spaced aggregate segment such as cost = sum exactly as the engine does
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 I-12 twin row (view.rs parse_col_aggregates vs queryViewProperties.ts / sheet/aggregate.ts query policy). The engine trims both sides of = (and master's parser agreed) but og's shared codec refused whitespace after =, so a block with tine.col-aggregates:: cost = sum showed the aggregate in the table while the Display editor did not see it and appended a duplicate cost=sum. One golden of 22 aggregate-list values is now read by the Rust parser and the TS codec; the D35 assertion that pinned the refusal now states the engine's rule.

coverage.failBefore: n/a: probe found no divergence; coverage extension only

entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 scanner row searchQuery.ts:59,96 (quoteDsl and the savedDslToFriendlySearch regexp read the DSL string grammar). Probed: both sides treat only backslash-quote and double-backslash as escapes and the engine reads the saved form back as one content-match over the trimmed source; no divergence. Pinned with a 12-case golden (Windows paths, trailing backslash, embedded newline, unicode) read by both suites.

entries.title: A BEGIN_QUERY block with a closing line ending or CRLF delimiters is a query in the editor as it is in export and publish
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 I-12 twin row (BeginQuery.tsx WHOLE_BEGIN_QUERY vs render.rs whole_begin_query_payload, a hand translation whose doc comment claimed JavaScript's terminal $ accepts one final line ending; it does not). Differences before: a block raw ending in one final line ending was a query natively but plain text in the editor, and a CRLF-delimited payload kept a stray CR in the frontend. The regexp now tolerates one final line ending and reads the payload lazily; a 29-case golden is read by both. render.rs gets only an additive test (outside the Q write set; the native function is unchanged).

entries.title: Copy and Export expand a tine-query macro as they expand a query macro
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 native/frontend scanner row ExportModal.tsx:143,388 (only the literal name query was warmed). A page with a tine-query macro (TQL) exported as the literal macro text: the export spec carried no dialect and the engine read every source as OG text. QueryExportSpec gains an optional dialect (absent = OG, so older callers and the IPC shape are unchanged); the export warms every query macro name through the one is_query_macro_name list and sends tql for tine-query; native export reads it through parse_query_text. Publish and rendered output already handled the name. Fail-before: the native export of a TQL source returned no blocks.

entries.title: A multi-word tag stays one member in formulas, table chips and board cards
entries.notes: Checkpoint-5 row formulaEval.ts:113,117 + fields.ts:225 (tags joined with a space then split on whitespace). A tag such as [[big idea]] became two formula list members (contains(tags, "big idea") false) and two chips in table cells and board cards. FieldValue now carries the parser-split members (items); the formula conversion, cell chips and board chips read them; the legacy raw split remains only for values without items. The live-document and DTO field readers were two copies of one switch (fields.ts readField, formulaEval.ts readFormulaRowField): both now call fieldValueFromFacets. Also repairs a tsc duplicate-import error left in queryBuilder.test.ts by the earlier golden commit.
